questions.explanation: Redundant links, devices and power supplies remove single points of failure, but they must be arranged so failures are truly independent; two paths through the same device share a common cause. Redundancy also introduces loops and convergence behaviour that must be managed and tested. A backup path that has never been exercised is not evidence of resilience. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
questions.hint: Ask what single failure would still stop the service.
questions.learningObjective: identify and explain redundancy using a packet-level scenario

options.text: Redundancy removes the need for testing failover.
Redundancy means duplicating only the backup power supply.
Redundancy eliminates all downtime.
Redundancy adds alternative paths and devices so a single failure does not take down the whole service.
